name: User Agent Parser
description: Parse any browser user-agent string into browser name/version, operating system, and device type — pre-filled with your own browser's user-agent.

faq.question: Why does an Edge or Chrome user-agent also contain the word Safari?
faq.answer: Both are built on WebKit-derived rendering engines and keep the historical "Safari" and "AppleWebKit" tokens in their user-agent for website compatibility — many older sites checked for that substring to decide whether to serve WebKit-friendly content. This tool checks for Edge's and Chrome's own more-specific tokens first, so it correctly reports "Edge" or "Chrome" rather than misreading them as Safari.

faq.question: Can this tell Windows 10 apart from Windows 11?
faq.answer: No — both versions report the identical "Windows NT 10.0" in their user-agent string, so there's no way to distinguish them from this data alone. This is a real limitation of user-agent strings, not something a better parser could fix.
